title: THC, CBD and the Minor Cannabinoids | The Bridge
h1: THC, CBD and the Minor Cannabinoids
description: THC and CBD get top billing, but the plant makes over 100 cannabinoids. Who CBG, CBN, CBC and THCV are, and what nobody can honestly promise yet.
lede: The plant makes more than a hundred cannabinoids and two of them get nearly all the press. Meet the rest, without the sales pitch.
html:
Read a lab report like a cast list. THC and CBD get top billing, but New York's regulator counts more than 100 cannabinoids in the plant, and more products now sell you the supporting cast by name. Some of that is real chemistry. Some of it is marketing running well ahead of the evidence.

THC, the headliner

Delta-9 THC is the primary psychoactive cannabinoid in the plant and the reason anyone uses the word high. It tends to bind to CB1 receptors, which affect the parts of the brain that regulate appetite, memory, fear and movement. More is not automatically better: the state's guide says a higher amount can raise the chances of paranoia or a rapid heart rate. Our Facts page walks through the receptor system if you want the fuller picture.

CBD, the second name

CBD is the second most prevalent cannabinoid, and unlike THC it does not cause a high by itself. That doesn't make it nothing. The National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health lists possible side effects including decreased alertness, changes in mood, decreased appetite and diarrhea, and says CBD use has been associated with liver injury and interactions with other drugs. If you take medication, tell your doctor. The same page notes that the FDA has not approved the cannabis plant for any medical use, and the FDA itself says only one CBD drug product has its approval, a prescription medicine.

The acids, where it starts

The plant doesn't build most of this directly. Cannabis makes mainly the acid forms: THCA, CBDA and CBGA. Smoking, vaping or baking converts them into THC, CBD and CBG. CBGA is the precursor molecule for both the THC and CBD branches of the family. That's why decarboxylation gets its own page here.

The supporting cast

  • CBG. Formed from CBGA through decarboxylation. In lab assays it shows weak activity at both main cannabinoid receptors.
  • CBN. The plant doesn't make it. It forms as THC degrades under light and heat, so it turns up in greater amounts in aged cannabis. It gets marketed as "the sleepy cannabinoid in old weed," but a 2021 review in Frontiers in Pharmacology calls the laboratory sleep results equivocal.
  • CBC. Another one the plant builds itself. Breeders have developed varieties rich in it, along with CBG, THCV and CBDV.
  • THCV. Two carbon atoms shorter than THC. It binds the CB1 receptor with significantly less activity than THC does, and it is considered rare.

Keep that same review's summary in your head when a package promises a specific mood: to date, it says, none of the minor cannabinoids have been clinically demonstrated to act as psychotropic drugs. Researchers are still working out what these compounds do, and plenty of that work so far happens in cells and rodents rather than people.

Delta-8 is a different conversation

Delta-8 THC isn't found in significant amounts in the plant, so concentrated versions are typically manufactured from hemp-derived CBD. The FDA says it has intoxicating effects similar to delta-9, and that delta-8 products have not been evaluated or approved for safe use in any context. The agency logged 104 adverse event reports between December 2020 and February 2022. New York's 2021 law counts delta-8 and delta-10 in its definition of THC.

What to do with all this

Use the names to read a lab report, not to buy a promise. The Certificate of Analysis shows which cannabinoids are present and in what amounts. A ratio like 1:1 tells you the proportion of THC to CBD, not the milligrams, so look for both. And write down what you tried and how it went. The state's guide includes journal pages for exactly this, because the same product doesn't affect everyone the same way.
